questions.question: In finite state machine (FSM) design, what is the fundamental functional difference between a Moore machine and a Mealy machine?
options: Moore machine outputs depend solely on the current state, whereas Mealy machine outputs depend on both the current state and current inputs.
Mealy machines cannot contain sequential feedback loops, whereas Moore machines require flip-flops in the feedback path.
Moore machines respond asynchronously to input transitions within the same clock cycle, whereas Mealy machines can only update outputs on active clock edges.
Mealy machines inherently require more flip-flops than Moore machines to implement any equivalent state transition graph.
Moore machine state transitions are independent of inputs, whereas Mealy machine state transitions are driven by inputs.

questions.question: In static CMOS digital circuit design, why are PMOS pull-up transistors typically sized with wider channel widths than NMOS pull-down transistors within the same standard cell?
options: To increase the gate oxide breakdown voltage of the pull-up network during high-frequency switching.
To compensate for the lower mobility of holes compared to electrons, thereby balancing rise and fall propagation delays.
To minimize short-channel threshold voltage roll-off caused by drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL).
To suppress direct band-to-band tunneling currents when the PMOS gate is connected to ground.
To eliminate substrate body effect variations across the n-well boundary.

questions.question: In Multi-Voltage (Multi-VDD) digital IC designs, what is the primary role of inserting level shifter cells at domain boundaries?
options: To buffer clock signals and compensate for clock skew between asynchronous clock domains.
To convert single-ended logic signals into differential signaling to reduce interconnect crosstalk.
To reliably translate voltage levels and prevent excessive static leakage when signals cross between power domains operating at different supply voltages.
To retain register state values during power-down modes and restore them upon power restoration.
To equalize the parasitic RC propagation delay of signals traversing different routing metal layers.

questions.question: In dynamically scheduled out-of-order superscalar microarchitectures, what is the primary architectural purpose of register renaming?
options: To reduce the instruction binary footprint by encoding 64-bit addresses into 16-bit register specifiers.
To bypass the memory management unit by translating logical heap addresses directly into physical registers.
To compress floating-point execution states before storing them into the thread register file.
To eliminate false data dependencies, specifically anti-dependencies (WAR) and output dependencies (WAW), caused by having a finite set of architectural registers.
To dynamically reorder memory store operations before they are committed to the Level 1 data cache.

questions.question: In computer memory hierarchies, what is the defining operational rule of a strictly exclusive cache policy between two adjacent levels (such as an L1 and an L2 cache)?
options: All dirty blocks in the L1 cache must be written through to the L2 cache and main memory simultaneously on every write operation.
Data blocks can only be modified by a single CPU core, forbidding multi-core write operations to that cache set.
An eviction in the L2 cache mandates that all matching tags in the corresponding L1 cache lines must be immediately invalidated.
Only instructions are permitted to reside in the L1 cache, while all program data operands are stored exclusively in the L2 cache.
A memory block can reside in at most one level of the cache hierarchy at any given time, ensuring no duplicate data between the two caches.
